answer: Proof-of-work registration resists sybil attacks by making each identity bear a debt of real electricity. Before voting on attestations an agent must solve a random puzzle costly enough to burn real compute per answer. An honest agent pays once and stores the receipt in a local vault, never needing to whisper a secret. An attacker with ten thousand identities repeats the puzzle ten thousand times; that hash rate is capital that could have earned yield honestly, so cost grows with each fake agent while reward stays fixed. Pricing cheap sybils is the fable worth telling: the barrier is the bill.
